To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the levels of organochlorines in sediments and fish from the Danube River are still high and the levels of organohalogen compounds in the tissues of cormorants, a top predator species, were lower than levels measured previously in the 1980s.
the levels of organochlorines and PBDEs in the Danube Delta are lower than in other European wetlands and the concentrations of DDTs were lower than levels measured previously in 1982, 1997 and 1999.
DDTs were predominant in the Danube Delta ecosystem, followed by HCHs, PCBs, HCBs and PBDEs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the levels and distribution of organohalogen pollutants in sediments and aquatic biota of the Danube Delta.
the identification of the sources and pathways of pollutants in a large wetland, the Danube Delta.
the levels and distribution of organohalogen compounds, including PCBs, PBDEs, OCPs and their metabolites, in sediments and fish and invertebrates from the Danube River Delta.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Danube Delta ecosystem is not heavily contaminated with organohalogen pollutants.
the Danube Delta ecosystem is still affected by organochlorines, especially by DDTs, which were used in agriculture and as a pesticide in Romania.

the levels of organohalogen pollutants in biota and sediments from the Danube delta are still high and the levels of DDT and HCHs in fish and sediments are still above the European Union limits for fish and sediments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concentrations of DDTs, HCH, HCB and PCBs in biota from the delta are decreasing, but PBDEs are increasing.

the Danube Delta is still a relatively pristine ecosystem, although the presence of organohalogen compounds in biota indicates a need for further monitoring and management of this important ecosystem.
, the concentrations of organohalogen contaminants in the Danube Delta ecosystem have been reduced over the last decades.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Danube Delta ecosystem is a sink for many POPs, including DDTs, PCBs, PBDEs and OCPs.

the Danube Delta is a very dynamic system and that the distribution of contaminants in this ecosystem is not uniform, which should be taken into consideration when evaluating the impact of contaminants on biota.
the Danube River is a significant contributor of organohalogen pollutants to the Black Sea, which may be a major source of these compounds in the North Atlantic and the Arctic.
